rationale: Since RANK(NEG(x)) = 1 − RANK(x), the expression algebraically collapses to RANK(re/at) − RANK(asset growth), so it contains no interaction at all and is simply a linear combination of two well-known published anomalies (asset growth and retained-earnings/profitability quality), contradicting its stated "composite" mechanism.

The construction is internally consistent and the sign is coherent, but it is a fairly derivative member of the archive's "spend/finance × weak-OCF" family and its two legs are individually known anomalies (net external financing, cash-flow profitability), so incremental content is uncertain and sstk-driven coverage should be checked.

The conditioning variable is mechanically induced by the primary variable — growing ppent directly depresses the trend in sale/ppent — so the product largely reduces to a convex transform of PPE growth rather than a genuine capacity-utilization interaction, and it is otherwise a near-cosmetic swap on the archive's already-weak DeterioratingMarginPPEBuild.

A legitimate, economically distinct conditioning variable (working-capital cushion rather than margin) applied to the inventory-growth channel, though it remains a modest refinement of the archive's LowMarginInventoryBuild and risks loading on known accrual/NWC effects.

Genuinely novel and internally consistent interaction with a plausible asymmetry story, but the test should verify it is not simply proxying the net-share-issuance anomaly among cash-burning small firms.

The spread again collapses algebraically to RANK(MA(oancf/at)) − RANK((capx−dp)/at), i.e., a plain profitability-minus-investment composite that is close to a hand-rolled RMW/CMA combination and thus likely absorbed by the FF5 benchmark, with no conditioning mechanism actually implemented.
